title: Drought turnover contrasts had intervals across zero in four Cedar Creek planting-group and period tests in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether drought reduced annual change in functional group biomass shares at Cedar Creek. Four paired tests used four- and 16-species plantings in 2017-2019 and 2020-2022. The panel had 432 records from 18 whole plots and 72 subplots. Drought-minus-control total variation contrasts were -0.0720, +0.0075, -0.0554 and +0.0481. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Hellinger distance, endpoint change and heat interactions did not establish a repeated effect. A triangle-inequality bound showed that small hypothetical errors in annual composition can remove sign certification for the descriptive contrasts. These error levels are not estimated sampling errors. Moving harvest strips, few plots, broad groups and one site limit inference. Periods reuse plots and do not give independent regional replication. This follow-up uses the same release as prior campaign diversity studies but tests composition change. Code, aggregate results, a figure, checks, source hashes and an external retrieval script are included. Raw data remain external.

display.caption: Four drought contrasts in annual functional group turnover. All adjusted plot intervals include zero. The tests use one site and repeated plots.
